svg.title: Voider architecture, authenticated transports, integrity and USB pairing
svg.desc: Phone dial targets have separate straight arrows. Each isolated namespace bridge labels its .2 endpoint above and its .1 endpoint below. Internet and calls remain off until both boot checks pass. WireGuard authenticates with paired keys; Tor uses two bidirectional authenticated streams.
svg.text: Private phone-to-phone calling · Raspberry Pi · Alpine Linux aarch64
SIP rewrite / NFQUEUE → vethX bridge → netnsX / wgX
10.X.1.1 selects local slot X · one isolated tunnel per imported server
10.1.s.1 selects a paired client by certificate index s
wgX UDP sockets stay in default netns · NOTRACK / stateless SIP rewrite · Tor SOCKS: 172.30.255.1
SFTP over Tor · separate account / key path / chroot
Incoming CAP2 uses client accounts; server accounts have no authorized key.
Pair-secret HMAC · same XID · atomic RAM records · size / count / TTL limits
LAN WG → direct WG → punch → Tor
Selection order; keep a healthy path.
02 / AUTHENTICATE THE PATH BEFORE CARRYING CALLS
Paired public keys + WG shared secret
Handshake + tunnel ping → enable call route
Tor secret + USB fingerprint → HMAC authentication
Tor encrypts · 2 bidirectional streams · first valid copy wins
03 / BOOT GATE · INTERNET + CALLS OFF UNTIL BOTH CHECKS PASS
04 / USB PAIRING · PRIVATE HANDOFF → VALIDATE → SAVE
Checksum verifies the copy; trust comes from the private USB handoff.
X and s are independent · keep s from the bundle
